message.content:
Since \(ab\) is invertible modulo \(n\), both \(a\) and \(b\) are invertible modulo \(n\). Thus \(a^{-1}\) and \(b^{-1}\) exist.

We use the identity
\[
a^{-1}+b^{-1}=(a+b)(ab)^{-1}\pmod n,
\]
because
\[
(a+b)(ab)^{-1}=a(ab)^{-1}+b(ab)^{-1}=b^{-1}+a^{-1}.
\]

Therefore,
\[
(a+b)^{-1}(a^{-1}+b^{-1})
\equiv (a+b)^{-1}(a+b)(ab)^{-1}
\equiv (ab)^{-1}
\pmod n.
\]

Given \((ab)^{-1}\equiv 2\pmod n\), the expression is congruent to \(2\pmod n\).

The answer is 2.
